cards.power: Autogenesis: Player creates a new rule from thin air.
cards.lore: Created himself to avoid paying union dues to parents. The ultimate freelancer.
cards.gradeReason: Make your own rule on the spot — purest improv invitation in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Comic mythological wrestling. Subject: Frog-headed god emerging from void. Mood: Smug self-creation.

cards.power: Reset Board: Flush all active cards. Return to the void.
cards.lore: Infinite dark water. The unscripted pre-show where nothing matters.
cards.gradeReason: All-? stats create table debate; reset-the-void power is evocative but opaque.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Cosmic horror wrestling poster. Subject: Dark primordial ocean swallowing cards. Mood: Eerie void.

cards.power: Wall of Wind: Blocks all flying attacks. Separates tag teams.
cards.lore: Got the job of holding his kids apart. Literally the atmosphere in the room.
cards.gradeReason: Tag team separation mechanic is clear but requires partner context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Cartoon mythology. Subject: Wind god holding two wrestlers apart. Mood: Breezy chaos.

cards.power: Corrosive Spit: Destroys one Equipment Card.
cards.lore: Born from a god's sneeze. Moisture farming with extreme prejudice.
cards.gradeReason: Clear destructive action but depends on Equipment cards being in play.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Vicious cartoon. Subject: Lion-headed goddess spitting acid at a weapon card. Mood: Ruthless.

cards.power: Earthquake Laughter: Shake the table. If cards fall, they are destroyed.
cards.lore: The Earth Father. His laugh destroys cities. Has a goose on his head for reasons.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Seismic chaos wrestling. Subject: Earth god laughing, table vibrating, cards flying. Mood: Gleeful destruction.

cards.power: Star Fall: Drop a handful of tokens. Damage equals hits.
cards.lore: The Sky Mother. Eats the sun every night. Digesting a star is heartburn central.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Celestial myth art. Subject: Star-covered goddess arching over ring, dropping tokens. Mood: Cosmic indifference.

cards.power: Executive Order: Change the turn order. It's good to be the King.
cards.lore: Travels the sky in a yacht. Has a lion to eat humanity because they stopped clapping.

cards.power: Resurrection Roll: Retrieve one card from your discard pile.
cards.lore: Moves the sun by treating it like a ball of poop.

cards.power: Undying Popularity: Cannot be eliminated. Just moves to the "Dead" pile and keeps scoring.

cards.gradeReason: Immortal wrestling champ who never leaves — Undertaker archetype, zero explanation needed.

cards.power: Gather the Pieces: Reassemble a destroyed card.

cards.power: Sandstorm Sabotage: Blind an opponent for one turn.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Calendar mythology. Subject: Thoth at gambling table winning days from calendar god. Mood: Triumphant technicality.

verdict: The Pharaoh Piledriver is a mythology-teaching machine disguised as a chaos generator — every single Egyptian god gets a wrestling archetype so accurate it feels like the original job title. SET (THE HEEL) is the deck's crown jewel: "Chaos Aardvark. Killed his brother over a chair shot. We all hate him; he loves it" is the most complete villain promo in any Kayfabizarro deck. Weakness: the Architects Daughter font-mode cards on pages 7 and 12 feel like a different production pass than the rest, and RENENUTET's "Harvest Gold" is the only power that could be from any card in any game. The Banger section (locations and events drawn from actual myths) is criminally good — THE LETTUCE INCIDENT and THE RED BEER TRICK alone justify purchase. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: 52 Egyptian gods, monsters, and cosmic events reborn as wrestling archetypes. For mythology fans, history teachers, and anyone who's wanted to end civilization with APEP (THE GLITCH).

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: PHARAOH PILEDRIVER – The Egyptian Pantheon, Booked as a Wrestling Roster (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

The Egyptian gods were running a wrestling promotion the whole time. Same egos, bigger hats, no off-season.

Walk into the locker room and the booking sheet explains itself. RA (THE CEO) runs the show from a yacht and reshuffles the turn order the second the crowd stops clapping. OSIRIS (THE ZOMBIE CHAMP) got boxed, drowned, and chopped into pieces, and still draws the loudest pop in the building because he flatly refuses to stay dead. SET (THE HEEL) killed his own brother over a chair shot, and we hate him for it, which is precisely the reaction he books. SHAI (DESTINY) writes the finish before the dice even hit the table, because you cannot fight the booking committee. Five thousand years of mythology, and every god already had a gimmick. Nobody had to invent one.

So you take ISIS (THE FIXER), or SOBEK (THE TEETH) who "eats tourists, a complex guy," and you perform the god out loud while the table rules whether you booked the match or just got booked. That is Social Story Wrestling: 52 cut-and-play cards that turn the whole Egyptian cosmos, gods, monsters, sacred venues, and the genuinely stupid things that happened in the actual myths, into a roster you can shuffle, deal, and argue about at table distance.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Pharaoh Piledriver Core Deck: 52 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards. You perform SET (THE HEEL), the chaos aardvark who loves that you hate him; APEP (THE GLITCH), whose System Crash ends the entire game so nobody wins unless RA is on the table; and BABI (THE ALPHA), whose whole instruction is "Attack immediately. Ask questions never."
- The Freestyle Rules: the complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and instructions you physically have to do, like GEB (THE FLOOR), who has you shake the table until cards fall off and die, and BES (THE MASCOT), who has you dance until the table laughs too hard to take its turn.
- The Myth-Banger pages: the real events, pulled straight from the source. THE LETTUCE INCIDENT, THE RED BEER TRICK, and a censored fish that ate the one piece of Osiris nobody could find a replacement for. These need no rulebook. The myth already did the work.

THE "LIVING DECK" PASS (Free Updates)
Grabbing this deck is not buying a static PDF. It plugs you into the Kayfabizarro historical cycle, the same workshop that drags Greek phalanxes, German epics, and dead philosophers onto the mat. Every future expansion and companion deck in this cycle lands in your library as a free update. The roster only gets deeper.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
I draw dead gods for a living, and I will not let a single one of them stay boring on the page. Every culture buries its pantheon under reverence until the characters suffocate; this deck digs them back up and makes them wrestle. Broke, a history teacher, a fourteen-year-old who just found Egyptian myth on the internet at 2am? Enter "0" and take it. Cut it, play it, teach with it. Want to fund the next pantheon? Every dollar goes straight into the next set of cards. It is all yours under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: share freely, attribute honestly, never resell.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
The gods never died. They just changed gimmicks and waited for someone to book them again.
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
